ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two sufficiently large charged parallel plates placed vertically form a uniform electric field region with a horizontal rightward direction, where the field strength is $E = 3 \times 10^4 \text{N/C}$. A small charged ball with mass $m = 5 \times 10^{-3} \text{kg}$ is suspended between the plates using an insulating thin string. When the ball is at rest, it deviates from the vertical direction by an angle $\theta = 60^\circ$ (with $g = 10 \text{m/s}^2$).

1. The electrical property and charge quantity of the small sphere; do not add any other content.
2. The tension in the suspension line.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
The small sphere carries a positive charge with a magnitude of $\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{3}\times10^{-6} \mathrm{C}$.
0.1 N

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two vertical parallel metal plates; the left plate is marked with “+”, and the right plate is marked with “-”, indicating that the electric field between the plates is from left to right. A small ball is suspended between the two plates by an insulating thin string. A vertical dashed line is drawn below the suspension point. The thin string deviates to the right from this vertical direction, with the angle marked as θ, and the small ball is located on the right side of the dashed line. Reasoning: The problem gives E=3×10^4 N/C, m=5×10^-3 kg, g=10 m/s^2, θ=60°. The small ball is stationary and deflects to the right, which shows that the electric field force it receives is to the right; the electric field is also to the right, so the small ball is positively charged. When the forces are balanced, in the vertical direction T cosθ=mg, and in the horizontal direction T sinθ=qE. Dividing the two equations gives tanθ=qE/(mg), so q=mg tan60°/E=(5×10^-3×10×√3)/(3×10^4)=5√3/3×10^-6 C. The tension T=mg/cos60°=(5×10^-3×10)/(1/2)=0.1 N.
